notes: §1985:XII.2.3 SR8: 'The implementor must allow a length from 1 through 322 characters for a text word within pseudo-text and within library text.' The one limit is MaxTextWordLength (65,535), checked for library text in CopyProcessor#ResolveOneCopy and for pseudo-text in ScreenOperandPair, at every edition, so every 1-322 character text word is allowed at --std 85 (allowing more is within 'must allow'). Probes at 85: a 322-character word continued over six lines in library text, replaced through a 322-character pseudo-text-1 word (also continued), prints LONG OK; a 1-character word Q replaced prints ONE OK; a 400-character pseudo-text-2 word is accepted by the text stage (the parse then refuses the non-statement it forms); a 160-character continued literal in pseudo-text-2 displays whole. The witness is a 162-character literal text word in library text.

next.reason: 1985: "The implementor must allow a length from 1 through 322 characters for a text word within pseudo-text and within library text."; 2023: "The length of a text-word within pseudo-text and within library text shall be from 1 through 65,535 character positions.". Same subject, but the limit rises from 322 to 65,535. Text words of 323 to 65,535 characters, which 1985 did not require compilers to allow, must now be accepted.
